label: 30 Days
title: Foundation Phase
goal: Build the habit and learn correct movement before adding heavy load.

weeks.training: 3 sessions: full-body, light load, focus entirely on technique for squat, hinge, push, pull, carry.
weeks.diet: Track your current intake without changing anything yet — you need a real baseline before adjusting.
weeks.milestone: You can rack, brace, and perform each basic lift without coaching cues.

weeks.training: 4 sessions: add light load increases (5–10%), introduce the warm-up routine as a non-negotiable first step.
weeks.diet: Set your protein target (1.6g/kg) and hit it daily — this is the single highest-leverage change available.
weeks.milestone: Four sessions completed without a missed day.

weeks.training: 4 sessions: progressive overload begins — small, consistent weight increases week over week.
weeks.diet: Add a structured pre- and post-workout meal around training sessions.
weeks.milestone: Noticeable improvement in confidence under the bar, even if the weight is still light.

weeks.training: 3 lighter sessions, full mobility day added. This week resets fatigue before phase two.
weeks.diet: Review two weeks of food logs with a trainer; adjust calories based on actual progress, not guesses.
weeks.milestone: Baseline measurements taken: weight, key lifts, progress photos, energy levels.

label: 60 Days
title: Build Phase
goal: Increase strength and conditioning meaningfully while keeping recovery on track.

weeks.training: Move to a 4-day split (upper/lower/push/pull). Loads should be 10–15% heavier than your week-4 numbers.
weeks.diet: Recalculate calories based on updated bodyweight; increase protein slightly if training volume has grown.
weeks.milestone: First lift PR since the foundation phase — even 2.5kg counts.

weeks.training: Add one HIIT or conditioning session per week alongside strength days — this should feel hard, not comfortable.
weeks.diet: Introduce carb cycling: higher carbs on lift days, moderate on rest days.
weeks.milestone: Resting heart rate trending down across the week.

weeks.training: Full assessment week: retest your major lifts, log new numbers against week 4's baseline.
weeks.diet: Full check-in with measurements and photos compared against day 1.
weeks.milestone: Visible technique improvement on video comparison from week 1.

label: 90 Days
title: Transformation Phase
goal: Push toward your specific goal — strength, size, or fat loss — with a plan tuned to what's working.

weeks.training: Split adjusts toward your specific goal: heavier/lower-rep for strength, higher volume for size, or added conditioning for fat loss.
weeks.diet: Calories and macros tightened toward the specific goal — surplus, deficit, or recomp maintenance.
weeks.milestone: Program now feels personalized rather than generic — adjustments are based on your own data.

weeks.training: Highest-intensity block of the program. This is where most of the visible transformation happens.
weeks.diet: Tightest adherence window — this is the two weeks where consistency matters most.
weeks.milestone: Noticeable physical change visible in photos, not just numbers.

weeks.training: Deload week, full lift retest, and a session reviewing form on camera one more time.
weeks.diet: Final measurements, full comparison against day 1, and a maintenance plan built for after day 90.
weeks.milestone: Complete before/after comparison: strength numbers, body measurements, and a plan to keep the results.
